text:
sam: Heads-up — we're hitting pretty bad late-enrich backpressure on attribute lookups during the evening spike. Lots of cache misses for billing_key/envelope stitching and the downstream enrichment fanout is spiking CPU. Thoughts on trading precision for resilience?

maria: ugh. can you paste a small example of the failure mode and the metrics? is it a read latency issue or queue depth? :thinking_face:

sam: quick paste from the ingest logs + metrics snapshot:
```
WARN 2026-03-20T23:02:11Z ingest-service lookup_timeout tenant=acme-msq latency=1200ms cache_hit=false queue_depth=512
metric.enrich.lookup.latp50=800ms
metric.enrich.lookup.errors=2.3%
```
queue grows -> connector times out -> we retry which multiplies the fanout.

ravi: sounds like classic thundering lookup. one pattern: cache-first stitching where we attach a best-effort attribute set from cache and mark the trace/span with stitch_status=approximate. then kick an async reconciliation job that backfills precise attributes later and emits a reconciliation event for billing re-eval. reduces tail latency and immediate fanout.

elena: that lowers tail latency but introduces eventual correctness for cost attribution. we need to define SLA for "approximate" vs "precise" attribution and how it shows up in the billing UI/charges. also need tests to prevent double-charge during reconciliation.

maria: agree. also we should consider tenant tiering: premium tenants get blocking lookups, standard tenants get cache-first. cheaper overall cost and less surface for SLOs. TTL on cached attrs + versioned attribute schema will help.

sam: question about backpressure behavior: when the lookup queue > X do we drop enrichment requests (emit placeholder attrs) or queue and risk OOM/backpressure propagation? i lean toward soft-fail + metric + trace flag so callers can decide.

ingest-bot: rate_limiter applied: tenant=acme-msq window=60s burst=100 -> 429s emitted

ravi: pattern i'd propose: circuit-breaker on external lookup. if queue/latency > threshold, attach cached attrs + set stitch_status=approximate or lookup_status=dropped_lookup. enqueue a low-priority reconciliation job (separate worker pool) and increment metric.reconcile.scheduled. we should also emit an audit trace/span so downstream billing can reconcile.

elena: for reconciliation we need an idempotent update path and a compact delta event (only changed billing_key/tenant attribution) so downstream processors can apply adjustments instead of reprocessing whole trace. deterministic fallback keys (hashed tenant+svc) can reduce misattribution noise when approximate attrs are used.

maria: i'll prototype a feature flag: `ingest.lookup.fallback_mode = [strict, cache_first, aggressive_cache]` with TTLs and tenant overrides. acceptance: (1) no end-to-end latency regression for 99th p50->p99, (2) reconciliation job runs under separate quota and has an SLA for completion, (3) billing report can accept delta adjustments.

sam: action items: maria to prototype flag + metrics, ravi to sketch worker pool + circuit-breaker thresholds, elena to write acceptance criteria for billing reconciliation and double-charge prevention. i'll open an RFC and tag the cost/finance and support folks. can we target a small beta next week? :thumbsup:

maria: yep, i can get a prototype up by EOD Friday — will add a quick dashboard for queue_depth/approximate_rate/reconcile_lag.

ravi: i'll push a design doc for the circuit-breaker and background reconciler. i'll include example pseudocode and failure modes.

elena: i'll draft the billing reconciliation contract and negative-charge guardrails.

sam: perfect. i'll file the RFC and add a checklist. thanks everyone — this should reduce the tail amplification and give us a safe path to keep the ingest pipeline stable while preserving attribution quality.
